clue.text: With time gone, terrible deficit facing European building

indicators.note: terrible suggests something wrecked, so the remaining letters are jumbled into a new order
With time gone says the letter standing for time is taken out of the word before it

explanation.surface: A grim financial shortfall threatens a European construction project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With time gone' drops just one of the two Ts; 'terrible' then rearranges what is left into EDIFIC, and 'facing' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An edifice is a large, imposing structure, so building is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Attraction with play on words in turn formulated

parts.note: a draw is something that attracts crowds

indicators.note: in turn says the word for wordplay is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: a pun is a play on words

explanation.surface: A show's appeal comes from its wit, cleverly worked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in turn' means the wordplay term is read backwards, giving NUP; 'formulated' is used in the sense of a plan being drafted.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan or document that has been drawn up has been drafted, i.e. formulated.

clue.text: A number provided in promotion for female

indicators.note: in a down clue promotion means raising, so the letters are written upwards, i.e. reversed

parts.note: if means provided, as in 'provided that'

explanation.surface: A figure is supplied in a marketing campaign aimed at women.
explanation.walkthrough: A + NO + IF gives ANOIF; 'in promotion' sends it up the grid, so it reads FIONA.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiona is a woman's given name, so a female is a fair crossword-style hint for it.

clue.text: Cold region in Italy, area with many lakes

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
Umbria is a region of central Italy

explanation.surface: A chilly part of Italy sounds like lake country.
explanation.walkthrough: CUMBRIA is the county in north-west England containing the Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lake District, England's main lakeland, lies in this north-western county.

clue.text: Expression of surprise about posh US city offering rich stew

indicators.note: about means going round, so the exclamation wraps around the other letters

parts.note: gosh is an exclamation of surprise
U is the old label for upper-class usage, i.e. posh
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: Someone gasps at a fancy American restaurant serving a hearty stew.
explanation.walkthrough: U for posh comes from the 'U and non-U' distinction of upper-class English speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Goulash is a Hungarian dish of meat and paprika, a thick hearty stew.

clue.text: Item in kitchen drawer in first section?

definitions.meaning: a tin or bottle ... is a utensil kept in a kitchen drawer
the opening part of something, such as a first match or opening act

explanation.walkthrough: Two senses: a kitchen gadget and whatever comes first, like a cricket opening batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a gadget for tins or bottles; the other is the initial part or item in a sequence.

clue.text: Delicate bachelor starts to use little burner — it glows?

parts.note: light means delicate, as in a light touch

indicators.note: starts to says take the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A fragile single man begins a small fire that shines.
explanation.definitionFit: A light bulb gives off a glow when switched on, so the question-marked description fits it.

clue.text: Section of an orchestra as could be pulled?

definitions.meaning: violins, violas, cellos and basses form a section of the orchestra
also literal cords that can be tugged

explanation.walkthrough: The second half plays on the idiom 'pull strings', to use influence behind the scenes.
explanation.definitionFit: The bowed instruments form one orchestral section, and cords are things one can tug.

clue.text: Act confidently in fearless tones possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Speaking in bold tones shows a person acting with confidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges all thirteen letters of FEARLESS TONES.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert oneself is to behave forcefully and confidently, insisting on one's rights.

clue.text: Glowing ring with a loft in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A shining circle hangs somewhere in an attic.
explanation.definitionFit: A halo is the luminous circle painted around a saint's head.

clue.text: Muddle with greens in a poor state for couriers

parts.note: a mess is a muddle

indicators.note: in a poor state suggests the vegetables are spoiled, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Delivery riders make a mess of wilted vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a poor state' reads as describing the vegetables but is the anagram signal, giving ENGERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Couriers carry and deliver messages or packages, the same job as these carriers.

clue.text: Entertainment in a field cancelling opening? It's not reasonable

indicators.note: cancelling opening says the first letter of the word for the entertainment is removed

parts.note: a funfair, with rides and stalls, is often set up in a field

explanation.surface: Calling off the start of an outdoor show seems unjust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' is a link word; the definition is 'not reasonable'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unjust or not fair is not reasonable, so the phrase is a synonym.

clue.text: Start to eye opening in good equestrian activity

indicators.note: Start to says take the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: a vent is an opening or outlet

explanation.surface: Someone spots a good gap in the course at a horse event.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventing is a horse-riding competition combining dressage, cross-country and show jumping.

clue.text: Increase the risks in haunt Pete constructed

indicators.note: constructed suggests something built up again, so the letters are assembled in a new order

explanation.surface: Building a haunted house for Pete raises the stakes.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from poker, where raising the stake makes the game more dangerous.

clue.text: Ambassador with view about India showing indecision

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the formal title of an ambassador

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for a view goes round the letter

parts.note: a stance is a view or position on something
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A diplomat dithers over his opinion of India.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesitance is reluctance or wavering before acting, which is indecision.

clue.text: Chaps in audience making appearance

indicators.note: in audience means as heard by listeners, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: guys are chaps, men

explanation.surface: Some men among the spectators make an entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearance' here means outward form, as in 'in the guise of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A guise is an outward semblance or form, as in disguise, so appearance fits.

clue.text: Fellow is given direction in banquet

parts.note: east is a compass direction

explanation.surface: A man is told which way to go at a formal dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A banquet is an elaborate formal meal, just like a lavish spread.

clue.text: Medical incident in part of a series

definitions.meaning: a bout or attack of illness, such as a psychotic or fainting attack
a single instalment of a television or radio serial

explanation.walkthrough: Two senses: a bout of illness and an instalment of a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctors call a single attack of illness by this word, and a TV instalment shares it.

clue.text: Eccentric sent a bike to get mixed drink

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: An oddball posts a bicycle in exchange for a cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: A snakebite is a British pub drink of lager mixed with cider.
explanation.definitionFit: The drink combines two beverages, lager and cider, in one glass, so it is a mixed drink.

clue.text: Sort wine of a similar sort

parts.note: a kind is a sort or type
red is red wine

explanation.surface: A type of wine resembles another of its type.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindred spirits are alike in nature, sharing a similar character.

clue.text: Performer wearing hat that is pleasant to touch

indicators.note: wearing means having something on, so the hat goes round the performer

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat
an act is a performer or group on a bill

explanation.surface: An entertainer in a hat that feels soft to the touch.
explanation.walkthrough: TILE for hat is dated British slang; T(ACT)ILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactile describes things that are agreeable to handle or that invite stroking.

clue.text: Modern headquarters having an exchange of parts

indicators.note: having an exchange of parts says the word's two halves swap places

parts.note: a centre is a headquarters, a main base of operations

explanation.surface: A modern office building has its rooms swapped round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having an exchange of parts' splits CENTRE into CENT and RE and swaps them.
explanation.definitionFit: Recent means happening lately, so new or modern rather than old.

clue.text: Inspector has to emphasise extreme sorrow

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector in British police ranks
to stress is to emphasise

explanation.surface: A police officer must stress how deeply grieved someone is.
explanation.definitionFit: Distress is anguish or acute suffering, which is extreme sorrow.

clue.text: Observe warning

definitions.meaning: to see or spot something, a verb

explanation.walkthrough: A verb sense and a noun sense of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to observe it, and advance notification is a warning.

clue.text: Vagrant close to last entry to a car park

indicators.note: close to says take the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: a ramp leads into a multi-storey car park

explanation.surface: A homeless person sits near the final way into the car park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to last' gives T, the end of 'last'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramp is a homeless wanderer with no fixed abode, a vagrant.

clue.text: One giving advice is elected local politician, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the word is given by how it is spoken

parts.note: a councillor is an elected member of a local council

explanation.surface: An adviser is said to be a member of the town council.
explanation.definitionFit: An adviser or therapist offers guidance to clients, so the description fits.

clue.text: Dry element in bar identified

indicators.note: element in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dry ingredient is spotted in a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'element' sounds chemical, but it just means a part of the words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Arid land gets almost no rain, so it is parched and dry.

clue.text: Figure still in filthy site

indicators.note: in says the word for still goes inside the word for the dirty place

parts.note: a sty, a pigsty, is a filthy place
even means still, as in even calmer

explanation.surface: A shape is still lurking on a dirty site.
explanation.walkthrough: EVEN means still in the sense of 'even better' or 'still better'.
explanation.definitionFit: Seventy is a number, and a numeral is a figure.

clue.text: Took up commercial work with Edward shortly

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
OP, short for opus, is a work
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Someone took on an advertising job with Edward briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: To adopt a cause or idea is to take it up and embrace it.
